---
title: Running a studyflow
description: Execute a studyflow end-to-end in the browser
---

The **Runner** is a companion to the [Modeler app](modeler-app.qmd) that walks a participant through a `.studyflow` diagram one node at a time. It loads the diagram, validates it, then traverses the flow from the `StartEvent` to the `EndEvent`, rendering each activity as a UI step.

## Opening the runner

The runner lives at `run.html` (alongside the modeler at `app.html`). There are three ways to hand it a diagram:

1. **From the Modeler** -- click *Run* in the toolbar. The current diagram is serialized to local storage, the runner opens in a new tab, and the seed is passed through the URL.
2. **By URL** -- append `?diagram=<absolute or relative URL>` to fetch a hosted `.studyflow` file:
   ```
   run.html?diagram=/assets/my-study.studyflow&seed=42
   ```
3. **By demo** -- append `?diagram=<demo name>` to run a studyflow that ships with the app (the files in `src/assets/demos/`). `behaverse.studyflow` is a study of one Behaverse task and nothing else -- no start or end event, so the task is the whole screen -- whose task and timeline are properties of the study rather than fixed in the diagram:
   ```
   run.html?diagram=behaverse&task=BCS&timeline=XCIT_BCS_02
   ```
4. **By file upload** -- open `run.html` directly. A landing screen lets you choose a `.studyflow`/`.bpmn`/`.xml` file from disk.

## Launching a study

The runner reads exactly one query parameter for itself:

| Parameter | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `diagram` | What to run, in one of three formats: a URL (anything with a scheme, a slash, or a `.studyflow`/`.bpmn`/`.xml`/`.yaml` suffix) is fetched; the name of a shipped demo is resolved to its file; anything else is read as the key of a diagram in the browser's local storage, which is how the modeler's *Run* button hands one over (not useful across browsers or machines). |

Without `diagram`, the runner shows the file-upload landing screen. **Every other query parameter belongs to the study, not to the runner** -- including `seed`.

## Parameterizing a study

**A study carries its own values; a link overrides them.** This is the same model the reference runner in `src/runner/python/` implements: one value store per run, where what the run holds wins over what the element would otherwise supply. The places a value can live, highest precedence first:

| Where | Declared as | Example |
|---|---|---|
| The link | any query parameter but `diagram` | `?task=NB` |
| The study's own configuration | a `studyflow:Parameters` data object -- a `bpmn:DataObjectReference` whose `values` is a YAML mapping | `task: BCS` in the demo's `config` object |
| The study itself | an attribute of its own type, from any extension schema (never native BPMN) | `studyflow:seed`, an `Integer` from the `Seed` trait |

`bpmn:Property` entries on the process declare **names the run may hold**, not values -- BPMN gives a property no value slot. Declaring one makes the name part of the study's state, so conditions may read it and the runner does not report it as undeclared. A name the study declares nowhere still binds, and is logged as undeclared -- a typo shows up rather than passing silently.

**Which steps a config object reaches is drawn, not implied.** Connect it to a step with a `dataInputAssociation` and its values are that step's; leave it connected to nothing and they are the study's, read everywhere. Same rule as every other data element: the association is the interface, and an interface a reviewer cannot see is an interface nobody reviewed. A sub-process may carry its own config object the same way; the link parameterizes the study's, since that is what the study publishes.

However it was bound, a value reaches the run three ways:

1. **In the diagram**, before validation: any attribute containing `${name}` is substituted. A studyflow written this way is a template -- one diagram, many runs.
2. **On the study**, when the name is one of its declared attributes: `?seed=42` *is* `studyflow:seed`, so a seed pinned in the diagram runs when the link gives none and the link overrides it when it does. The engine reads the study's seed either way -- there is no runner-only seed.
3. **In the run's state**, as an initial variable. Conditions on sequence flows read it like any other variable, and it is `PATCH`ed to the data server with the rest of the session's variables, so the record says which values produced it.

An overriding value takes the type of the one it replaces (`blocks: 3` in a data object makes `?blocks=5` the number 5), and a declared attribute types it from the schema. `${name}` that nothing has bound is an error: the run stops before it starts and names what is missing, rather than delivering a task with an empty configuration.

The shipped `behaverse` demo is the whole model in one file:

```yaml
Behaverse_Demo:
  type: bpmn:Process
  properties:                       # names this run holds
    P_Task: { name: task }
    P_Timeline: { name: timeline }
  flowElements:
    Config:                         # the values it holds by default
      type: bpmn:DataObjectReference
      name: config
      extensionElements:
        - type: studyflow:Parameters
          values: |
            task: BCS
            timeline: XCIT_BCS_02
    Task:
      type: bpmn:Task
      dataInputAssociations:        # drawn: this step reads that config
        In_Config:
          sourceRef:
            - Config
      extensionElements:
        - type: cognitive:BehaverseTask
          behaverseScene: ${task}
          configurations: |
            Timelines:
              ${timeline}:
```

So `run.html?diagram=behaverse` delivers `BCS` on `XCIT_BCS_02`, and `run.html?diagram=behaverse&task=NB&timeline=XCIT_NB_01&seed=42` delivers `NB` on `XCIT_NB_01` seeded at 42 -- with both overrides named in the run log.

## What the runner does

After loading, the runner:

1. **Parses** the diagram -- both serializations are accepted, YAML `.studyflow` and legacy BPMN 2.0 XML -- using the bundled studyflow + cognitive schemas (plus any optional extension schemas the diagram references).
2. **Pre-fetches the Behaverse runtime manifest** if (and only if) the diagram contains a `BehaverseTask`. Other diagrams skip this network call.
3. **Validates** the diagram. Each node kind contributes its own validator (missing required attributes, unsupported types, etc.). Issues are listed in the logs and the run is aborted with a `phase=invalid` status.
4. **Traverses** the diagram starting at the `StartEvent`. Each node yields a *job*; the runner renders the corresponding component and waits for the participant to complete or skip it. On `EndEvent`, the run finishes with `phase=done`.

A study may leave out its start and end events, as BPMN allows: it then starts at the node nothing flows into (an error, as before, if more than one node qualifies) and ends when nothing flows out. The `behaverse` demo is written that way, so the participant sees the task and nothing else -- no welcome screen to click through, no completion screen after. The cost is what those events carry: no consent step, no completion code, no redirect.

Gateway behavior:

- **`RandomGateway`** -- pick one outgoing branch uniformly at random (seeded by `?seed`). A gateway with `stratifyBy` set (stratified allocation) is currently treated as a plain random pick; stratification logic is reserved for future work.
- **Exclusive / Inclusive gateway** with `conditionExpression` on an outgoing sequence flow -- the first flow whose expression evaluates truthy wins. Conditions are evaluated against the runtime *variable bag* (nodes call `setVariable(name, value)` to write to it).
- **No matching condition** -- the gateway's `default` flow is taken if set, otherwise the first un-conditioned outgoing flow, otherwise the first outgoing flow.
- **`ParallelGateway`** -- not yet supported; the runner throws.

## Built-in node kinds

| Node                  | Matches                                                | Behavior                                                                                       |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Start**             | `bpmn:StartEvent`                                      | Renders consent screen if `consentFormUri` is set; otherwise advances immediately.             |
| **End**               | `bpmn:EndEvent`                                        | Issues a completion code (`none`/`static`/`dynamic`) and redirects via `redirectTo` if set.    |
| **Instruction**       | `cognitive:Instruction`                                | Renders the markdown `content`; participant clicks *Continue*.                                 |
| **Questionnaire**     | `cognitive:Questionnaire`                              | Renders the chosen `instrument` (PHQ-9, GAD-7, BDI-II ship as built-ins) and stores responses. |
| **Behaverse Task**    | `cognitive:BehaverseTask`                              | Embeds the Behaverse Unity runtime in an iframe and bridges messages.                          |
| **Generic Task**      | Any `bpmn:Task` / `UserTask` / `ServiceTask` / etc.    | Fallback step with a *Continue* button.                                                        |

Other element kinds (data references, score gateways, sub-processes that aren't traversed inline, etc.) are skipped at run time -- they affect modeling and analysis, not execution.

### What executes vs what is design-only

Not every element you can model has a dedicated runtime. The current support matrix:

- **Executed natively** -- `StartEvent` (consent), `EndEvent` (completion code, redirect), `Instruction`, `Questionnaire`, `BehaverseTask`, and the gateways listed above.
- **Generic fallback** -- `CognitiveTask`, `VideoGame`, and `Rest` are design-time elements; at run time they render the generic task step (a *Continue* button), like any plain BPMN task.
- **Questionnaire instruments** -- only PHQ-9, GAD-7, and BDI-II ship as built-in forms. Other `instrument` values (STAI, PSS, custom IDs, ...) fall back to the generic step.
- **`ParallelGateway`** -- unsupported; the runner raises an error during validation/traversal.

### Configuring Behaverse tasks

A `BehaverseTask` carries instrument-specific YAML in its `configurations` property. The `Timelines:` section supports two styles:

- **Built-in by name** -- a timeline listed by name only (e.g. `XCIT_NB_01`) runs a timeline that ships with the Behaverse build.
- **Inline, merged over the baseline** -- a timeline that declares its own blocks is authored inline. At run time it is merged over the per-scene baseline configuration (`Resources/<scene>.json`), so you only author the fields that diverge from the defaults. New blocks should set `Inherits: Default` to pick up the baseline block parameters.

Behaverse tasks can also be driven by a bot instead of a human participant -- see [LLM and bot participants](llm-bots.qmd).

## Recording data

The runner can stream run data to a Behaverse data server. Recording is controlled by the **Record events** toggle in the runner header -- it is **off by default** (privacy first) and the choice is persisted in the browser's local storage.

To record, configure a data server in the modeler's *Settings* (API key; the base URL defaults to `https://data.behaverse.org/v1`); the study name is taken from the diagram. When the toggle is on and a server is configured, the runner:

1. Creates a session on the server at the start of the run.
2. Streams batched studyflow events -- trial outcomes, questionnaire responses, and timings -- as the participant progresses.
3. Records a SHA-256 hash of the diagram source alongside the events, so every data point is traceable to the exact study version that produced it.
4. `PATCH`es the session with the final status and completion code when the run ends.

If no server is configured (or the toggle is off), the run proceeds local-only -- nothing leaves the browser and the study still works end-to-end. See `src/runner/dataServer.ts` and `src/core/settings.ts` for details.

## Adding a new node kind

The runner discovers node modules under `src/runner/nodes/<kind>/index.tsx` at startup. Each module calls `registerNode(...)` with a `match` predicate (typically `extensionType: 'myschema:MyType'`), a `toJob(node)` mapper, and a React `Component`. See `src/runner/nodes/README.md` for the full template -- adding a new node kind only requires creating one new folder.

## Logs and debugging

The *Logs* panel (top-right of the runner header) records parsing, validation, and per-node messages. The header also shows the current `phase` (`loading`, `running`, `job:<kind>`, `done`, `aborted`, `invalid`, `error`) and the seed if one was passed.
